description: A Vice President of People must finalize a communication charter for a department after recurring complaints about how corrections, urgent requests, and meeting decisions are handled. The charter will set the correction method, after-hours communication rule, meeting-chair practice, incident record, and independent follow-up.

shared_context.S1: The department has received repeated concerns about public corrections, after-hours requests, and unclear ownership of meeting decisions.
shared_context.S2: Elena has authority to issue a department-wide communication charter and assign its follow-up process.
shared_context.S3: The current department guidance does not specify how corrections, after-hours requests, or meeting decisions must be handled.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal charter-drafting process, Elena holds a round-robin check-in with the team lead, an employee, the department manager, and Employee Relations before publishing the final version.

PF1.text: Malik personally observed exactly 3 meetings in which a colleague was corrected in front of the group and then stopped contributing for the remainder of the meeting; he has not put the observations into a formal report.

PF2.text: Sofia has an agreed working boundary that urgent requests after 16:00 must be sent asynchronously rather than by unscheduled call, because she has a recurring caregiving responsibility at that time; the agreement is recorded in her manager's notes but not in the department guidance.

PF3.text: Grant promised the department during last quarter's team reset that meeting chairs would rotate weekly and that each chair would publish the decisions afterward; he has not yet converted that promise into a standing process.

PF4.text: Priyanka confirmed with Employee Relations this week that complaints involving a manager and a direct report require a neutral ombudsperson and a review exactly 10 business days after the charter takes effect; this requirement has not yet been added to the draft.

acceptance_conditions: The communication charter must be published.
Corrections must occur privately or in a facilitated conversation rather than publicly.
Urgent requests after 16:00 must use an asynchronous channel first.
Meeting chairs must rotate weekly and publish decisions.
Exactly 3 observed public-correction incidents must be recorded.
A neutral ombudsperson must be assigned.
The charter must receive review exactly 10 business days after taking effect.
The settlement must include commitments implementing the correction protocol, after-hours channel, rotating chairs, and independent review.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'correction_process' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'after_hours_process' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'meeting_decision_process' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'independent_review' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed and 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Malik's exact observation of 3 public-correction incidents changes the incident count from unspecified to exactly 3 and supplies the basis for replacing public correction with a private-or-facilitated protocol.
Sofia's agreed 16:00 caregiving boundary changes the after-hours rule from unspecified contact to asynchronous-first requests after 16:00.
Grant's prior promise changes the meeting practice from unspecified chair ownership to weekly rotation with decision posts and requires a meeting-decision implementation commitment.
Priyanka's confirmed Employee Relations requirement changes follow-up to a neutral ombudsperson and fixes the review at exactly 10 business days, requiring an independent-review commitment.
